idea: Home-style tiffin delivery for hostel students in Bidholi, Dehradun

strategist.problem: A hostel student in Bidholi finishes class at 6:30 PM, walks out and finds the mess food cold or the mess closed, and the nearby dhaba options are oily or ₹150+ per plate — the pain hits at dinner time when they're tired and don't want to decide or travel for food.
strategist.target_customer: Undergraduate and postgraduate students (18-24) living in private hostels and PGs around UPES Bidholi campus in Dehradun, with ₹8,000-15,000 monthly personal spend, who currently order Swiggy/Zomato or eat at a local dhaba 4-6 nights a week and would prepay a monthly plan for reliable home-style meals delivered to their hostel gate.
strategist.mission: Deliver affordable, home-cooked daily tiffin meals on a monthly subscription to hostel students near UPES Bidholi so they get consistent, hygienic dinner without deciding or travelling each night.

competitors.name: Local dhabas and small restaurants around Bidholi/RISE area
competitors.differentiator: We win on a fixed monthly price, predictable delivery to the hostel gate, and a rotating home-style menu instead of oily à-la-carte ordering each night.

competitors.name: Swiggy and Zomato delivery near UPES
competitors.differentiator: We win on per-meal cost under a monthly plan and on consistency of taste and hygiene, since they're ordering from a rotating set of unknown kitchens.

competitors.name: Hostel/PG in-house mess or tiffin providers run by local aunties in Bidholi
competitors.differentiator: We win on a simple digital subscription with UPI payment links, fixed delivery slots and menu variety, versus word-of-mouth-only messes with irregular billing.

scope_cuts: No custom mobile app or web ordering platform — a WhatsApp broadcast plus a Razorpay/UPI payment link handles ordering and collection until 50+ subscribers justify an app.
No in-house cooking kitchen or rented commercial space in month 1 — partner with one existing home-cook/tiffin service in the area on a per-meal rate so the founder never leaves classes to cook.

No delivery fleet or hired riders — the first 30 deliveries run on a single bicycle/scooter route done by the founder and one part-time batchmate, and we cut any multi-drop routing software until demand exceeds one route.

stack.name: WhatsApp Business
stack.why: Handles ordering, menu updates, and delivery confirmations directly in the students' existing chat app without a custom app.

stack.name: Razorpay
stack.why: Generates UPI payment links for monthly subscription collection, processing payments with a 2% + GST fee and no setup cost.

stack.name: Google Sheets
stack.why: Tracks the daily menu, subscriber list, and delivery route inventory using the free tier of Google Workspace.

stack.name: Canva
stack.why: Designs the weekly menu cards and WhatsApp status updates for the hostel groups using the free tier.

ai_tools.name: Gemini
ai_tools.why: Uses the free Google AI Plus student offer to draft WhatsApp menu messages and calculate per-meal food costs in Google Sheets.

ai_tools.name: Claude
ai_tools.why: Uses the free tier to write the standard operating procedure for the part-time batchmate handling the bicycle delivery route.

mvp_features: Lunch Tiffin: 1 rice, 2 seasonal vegetables, 1 dal, 1 seasonal fruit in a 750ml steel container
Dinner Tiffin: 2 rotis, 1 seasonal vegetable, 1 dal, 1 curd in a 750ml steel container
Monthly Subscription: 26 working days of delivery to the hostel gate with a fixed UPI payment link

tool_costs.price_note: 2% + GST per payment, no setup fee or AMC. Price checked 2026-11-02 on https://razorpay.com/pricing/

first_10_steps: Walk to 3 home-cook tiffin providers in the Bidholi area and negotiate a per-meal rate of ₹45 for a 750ml steel container with 1 rice, 2 vegetables, 1 dal, and 1 fruit.
Create a free WhatsApp Business account and set up a catalogue with 2 items: 'Lunch Tiffin' and 'Dinner Tiffin', including the exact ingredients and delivery time.
Generate a Razorpay payment link for a ₹2,600 monthly subscription (26 days x ₹100 per meal) and test it with a ₹10 UPI payment to verify the 2% + GST fee structure.
Use Canva free tier to design a 1080x1920 pixel menu card showing the 4-week rotating home-style menu and the ₹100 per meal price point.
Share the menu card and WhatsApp Business link in 5 UPES Bidholi hostel WhatsApp groups, targeting 50 students for a 7-day trial week.
Collect 10 pre-orders for the 7-day trial week (₹700 per student) via UPI to validate the ₹45 per-meal food cost and the ₹100 selling price.
Pick up the 70 tiffin containers from the home-cook partner at 1:00 PM and 6:00 PM, and deliver them to 3 specific hostel gates using a single bicycle route.
Use Claude free tier to write a 1-page SOP for the part-time batchmate detailing the exact pickup times, delivery sequence, and how to handle cold food complaints.
Track the 7-day trial in Google Sheets, recording the exact food cost, delivery time, and 3 customer feedback points per day to calculate the gross margin.
Convert the 10 trial students to a monthly subscription by sending a new Razorpay payment link for ₹2,600 on the 7th day, targeting 5 full subscriptions by week 6.

burn_line_items.item: Razorpay (2% + GST on collections, no fixed fee)
Marketing budget (menu card printing, WhatsApp group entry, ₹10 trial payments)

revenue_targets.notes: 10 trial students at ₹700 in week 1-2, 5 convert to ₹2,600 monthly by day 30; rest of trial revenue counted as one-time and not in MRR.
Second cohort from 5 more hostel WhatsApp groups; founder + 1 batchmate on one bicycle route still within capacity.
3 hostels covered, 18 full monthly subscribers; 2 on lunch+dinner blended into avg. Break-even already passed at 1 customer.

key_assumptions: Students near UPES Bidholi will prepay ₹2,600/month (₹100 per dinner) for 26 days — assumption based on target customer currently spending ₹150+ per plate at dhabas 4-6 nights a week, so monthly plan is a discount to current spend.
Home-cook partner delivers a 750ml tiffin at ₹45/meal landed cost including container, giving ₹55 gross margin per ₹100 meal before delivery labour.

delivery_cost_per_customer of ₹52 = ₹45 food+container + ₹7 per-customer share of bicycle wear, phone data and packaging tape. Delivery labour (founder's bicycle route and batchmate's help) is NOT deducted per-unit: founder is unpaid (own time, no stipend out of ₹15,000 capital) and the batchmate is paid in-kind with one free daily tiffin, whose ₹45 food cost is already inside the ₹45 goods line, so no separate cash burn line exists for delivery labour.
Razorpay 2% + GST fee is passed into the ₹45 food-cost line as a rounding allowance rather than a separate burn line since no fixed monthly fee exists.

channels.name: WhatsApp hostel/PG groups + broadcast near UPES Bidholi
channels.tactic: Join 12 named hostel and PG WhatsApp groups in Bidholi/RISE area (ask wardens and batchmates for invites), post the trial-week offer once per group on Sunday and Wednesday at 8 PM, then DM every reply individually with a Razorpay payment link for the ₹700 trial week; target 15 personal DMs/day and 3 trial signups/week from groups.

channels.name: Instagram Reels + First Dinner Free offer
channels.tactic: Post 1 Instagram Reel per day (15-second dinner tiffin pack-and-ride clip, CapCut free, caption with UPI link) targeting Bidholi student accounts, plus 3 evenings/week post a 'First Dinner Free' offer in 5 hostel WhatsApp groups for the first 5 students to claim; 30 DMs/day to interested students on sampling days.

first_10_customers: Day 1-2: List every hostel and PG within 2km of UPES Bidholi from Google Maps, walk into 6 of them, and ask the warden for the student WhatsApp group link; join at least 6 groups before posting anything.

Day 3: Post the trial-week message in all 6 groups at 8 PM, then reply personally to every 'price?' or 'veg?' question within 5 minutes; send the ₹700 Razorpay payment link to each person who engages.

Day 4-7: Deliver the first trial dinners yourself on a bicycle; ask each trial customer at the gate: 'If dinner is good tonight, will you take the ₹2,600 monthly plan on day 8?' — get the yes/no before they finish the trial week.
Day 8-10: Convert trial customers to monthly via UPI payment link; offer any student who refers a friend who pays ₹700 a free dinner on their next plan (revenue reduction, not spend).
Day 11-18: Walk into 4 more hostels, repeat the group-join + post + DM loop; personally call (not DM) the 8 students who replied but didn't pay and ask what stopped them.
Day 19-30: Post 1 Reel/day, run 3 gate sampling evenings, and push every paying monthly customer to add one batchmate from their own room floor — target 5 monthly subscribers by day 30.
growth.cold_message: Hi, I'm a UPES student starting a home-style dinner tiffin for hostels in Bidholi — 2 rotis, veg, dal, curd delivered to your gate by 8 PM, ₹2,600/month for 26 dinners (way under Swiggy). First week is a ₹700 trial so you can check the taste before committing. Want me to send the UPI link for a trial week starting tomorrow?

objections.objection: ₹2,600/month is too much, I can manage with the mess or Swiggy.
objections.response: Compare per dinner: ₹2,600/26 = ₹100 a night delivered to your gate, versus ₹150+ per dhaba plate or ₹200+ Swiggy orders 4-6 nights a week. Start with the ₹700 trial week — if you don't like the taste after 3 dinners, I refund the rest, no questions.

objections.objection: I don't know if the food will be good or hygienic — how do I trust you?
objections.response: Don't commit monthly yet. Take the ₹700 trial week: 7 dinners delivered to your hostel gate, and I'll share the home-cook's kitchen photos and this week's exact menu on WhatsApp before you pay. If dinner 1 isn't hot and fresh, I replace it that night free.

critic.verdict: This is a coherent, tightly-scoped plan that stays true to the home-style tiffin idea for UPES hostel students, with a realistic trial-week funnel, a credible ₹100/meal price point, and a founder-friendly stack of WhatsApp + Razorpay + Sheets. The scope cuts (no app, no kitchen, no delivery fleet) and the ₹15,000 bootstrapped capital are respected, and the campus-first WhatsApp channel matches the hard rules. The main open questions are around delivery capacity scaling and whether the trial-to-monthly conversion rate assumed is realistic without social proof.
critic.biggest_risk: The single biggest risk is that the founder's own bicycle delivery of 70+ tiffins/day (10 trial customers) plus classes exceeds the ~15 hours/week budget, causing late or cold deliveries in week 1 and killing word-of-mouth before any monthly subscriptions convert.
